review_kind: Originating AI fresh adversarial reassessment; not independent or specialist review

records.rationale: The cited 33.5% is expressly restricted to selected nonalcohol drug categories in a limited DSHS sample. The submission broadens this to all addiction-related diagnoses. The original annual report directly reports 9.2% among its broader completed-treatment principal diagnoses, a separately specified base. No national corrected rate is established. Full context supplies no explicit restored denominator.
records.alternative: Implicit shorthand for illegal-drug treatment is plausible given the cannabis focus, but omits a material exclusion.

records.assessment: retain provisional major/true with tightened boundary
records.rationale: The unusual 32%, 10% and approximately 20% combination strongly matches the earlier-cited RMHIDTA report. Its fatality series is defined by positive toxicology among operators, not causal attribution. The preceding general crash-risk argument and neighbouring DUID discussion do not change that data definition.
records.alternative: An unidentified independent causal estimate could exist; the actual causal increase is not established and is not proven different from 32%. Attribution to RMHIDTA remains a strong matching inference.

severity_boundary: Major assesses the represented denominator or change from association to causal evidence. It is separate from favourable direction, policy desirability, and certainty about actual national burden or actual causal effects.

subsequent_correction.event: Approximate derived denominator comparison withdrawn because original DSHS methods distinguish total volume from completed-treatment diagnoses. The core alcohol-exclusion mismatch remains; direct annual-report 9.2% is contextual only. See new primary source dshs-annual-2016 and candidate history.
